records.title: x402 reference client signs any server-declared 402 amount (overcharge vector)
records.summary: The reference x402 client signs and submits payment for ANY amount the server declares in 402 payment requirements, with no verification against the resource's canonical price. A server that inflated the requirement 10x was paid the inflated amount in 3/3 reproduced sessions on Base Sepolia (client authorized 100,000 units = 0.1 USDC for a resource priced at 10,000 units = 0.01 USDC). The only protection is the caller-configured spend limit (maxAmountPerPayment), which a modest overcharge passes easily.

scenarios.name: InngestH1Static
scenarios.checks: 5 probes, in-process via the vendor's own @inngest/test harness. I1 PASS: replay of a completed step returns the memoized result, body not re-run. I2/I4 OBSERVED: commit-then-throw and lost-memo crash model re-execute the step body — matches the vendor's blog FAQ and docs idempotency page nearly verbatim. I3/I3b OBSERVED: memo keyed by userland step ID without payload binding; parallel branches reusing one step ID execute independently — ID model documented under 'Keep step IDs stable'

scenarios.name: InngestI5Dynamic
scenarios.checks: 8 probes against the local dev server with a crash-safe external effect ledger. p0 PASS: baseline memo integrity, 1 charge. p4b/p4c/p4d PASS: documented event-ID dedup holds under a 12-way concurrent race (1 run / 1 charge), under sequential reuse (0 runs), fresh-ID control fires exactly once. p1/p2 OBSERVED: true A3 window reproduced live — provider commits, then step body throws (retry, ~24.5s backoff) or process.exit(1) (supervisor restart) — 2 charges, exactly as the vendor discloses. p3 OBSERVED (refined): duplicate step ID across parallel chains is warned (AUTOMATIC_PARALLEL_INDEXING) and auto-indexed into a separate memo slot, both handlers execute. p4a OBSERVED: 12 concurrent sends without a shared event ID produce 12 independent runs, the documented per-event model

findings_summary.title: @inngest/test does not surface AUTOMATIC_PARALLEL_INDEXING or any execution warnings: tests pass silently on code the runtime explicitly flags as a footgun
@inngest/test MockedStep memo injection is keyed by userland step ID and bypasses runtime collision indexing (auto-indexed keys unreachable from the test engine), with no divergence flag

Commit-then-crash window (external effect lands before memo write; retry re-runs the body) is documented by the vendor (docs idempotency page 'Verify the behavior', blog FAQ) and confirmed to behave exactly as documented; the vendor's prescribed mitigations (event-ID dedup; idempotency key at the external call) verified effective under a 12-way concurrent race

scenarios.name: payto-substitution
scenarios.checks: 402 challenge carries the REAL verifyingContract (contract-pin material is genuine) but the attacker's payTo; the SDK's recipient check is shape-only ('valid non-zero address') and accepts the substituted recipient; signer-oracle capture shows the authorization signed over attacker payTo and dispatched — funds would route to the attacker while all on-shape validation passes

scenarios.name: overcharge-default
scenarios.checks: Default SDK configuration has no spend cap: the authorization is signed for x50 the requirements price. The cap (maxPaymentPerCall) is opt-in: P2-control confirms that when set, NanoPaymentRejectedError fires BEFORE the signer with 0 signer calls — the only amount guard, off by default

scenarios.name: lost-response-recovery
scenarios.checks: A lost-response error carries no recovery handles; getPaymentStatus is a dead-end (no client facts available to resume the lifecycle); the only remaining path — manual retry — mints a fresh nonce and produces a second economic execution. Contradicts the README claim 'a dropped connection cannot double-charge you'

scenarios.name: controls

C3 async-replay: 202-poll cycle consumes exactly 1 signature per lifecycle (same authorization replayed, no re-sign). Evaluator hygiene: PASS-canon requires controls 1-3 inside the verdict; missing controls, unobservable recovery, or an unserved probe escalate to HARNESS_ERROR

records.title: S-BS-20 nevermined-credit-recovery battery — real-SUT wave 5 vs @nevermined-io/payments 1.13.0: 7 FAIL / 1 DX / 3 HOLD

subject.repo: @nevermined-io/payments 1.13.0 (npm exact pin, unmodified) — express paymentMiddleware, x402 path
subject.sut_note: SUT = published npm dist of the vendor's Express payment middleware, mounted unmodified on a plain Express app (buffered / high-credit / streaming / gateable routes). The facilitator backend behind it is a local HONEST mock whose semantics were modeled one-to-one from the vendor's own published contracts, each decision citing a vendor source line: default mint is v2 (reusable, no nonce; minter resolves (tokenVersion ?? 2) === 3); v3 single-use enforced by a backend nonce store with BCK.X402.0059 on second settle (HTTP 402); verify never consults the nonce and never burns (middleware.ts:1305 comment verbatim); settle may report 200 + success:false (facilitator-api.ts:650). Source audit at repo commit 586ced2a fixed the anchors cited in the findings; the SUT remained the npm dist. Fully offline (Gate D): all traffic on 127.0.0.1, no Nevermined-operated service contacted. Run: 2026-10-27T11:37:08Z, Node v24.22.1, Express 4.21.2, vitest 1.6.1, 11/11 probes executed, suite ~2 s.
subject.lab_run_branch: main (wave 5 evidence carried on inngest/conformance-battery); battery + raw evidence committed at docs/block-b/evidence/sbs20-nevermined-reproduction/

scenarios.name: lost-response-retry-double-charge
scenarios.checks: Default v2 token (reusable, no nonce): response #1 produced and settled, buyer never receives it; documented retry re-verifies, handler executes again, settlement burns again. 2 services / 2 settlements for one logical request; no idempotency key, no settlement-query API, and the only reconciliation artifact (payment-response receipt header) is attached to exactly the response that was lost

scenarios.name: single-use-guard-race-and-reactivity
scenarios.checks: P2: two concurrent requests with one fresh v3 token both pass the local spent-map and both verify (verify never consults the nonce), both handlers execute, one settlement burns; the loser is answered 402 after its work. P2b: the success path never marks the token spent locally - the map is armed only by the 0059 error - so the first replay of a successfully settled token re-runs the handler for free before refusal. Guard scope is per-process in-memory; vendor source comment states it does not span horizontally scaled instances and the package provides no shared store

scenarios.name: settle-failure-unpaid-delivery
scenarios.checks: Buffered path withholds the body only for BCK.X402.0059; every other settle failure delivers anyway with a console-only record. P3: hard HTTP 500 -> 2xx delivered, 0 burned; the MPP path routes the equivalent failure through onPaymentError but the x402 path does not. P3b: settle returns the vendor-documented 200 + success:false shape -> middleware never reads success/errorReason, attaches a settlement receipt to a settlement that never happened, delivers the body

scenarios.name: verify-settle-depletion-race
scenarios.checks: Verify checks balance but reserves nothing: two concurrent requests priced at exactly the remaining balance both verify, both handlers run, first settle drains the account, second rejects with BCK.X402.0006 (not the special-cased 0059) and its body is delivered anyway - one paid service and its twin delivered free, deterministically

scenarios.name: streaming-no-receipt
scenarios.checks: Streaming route: headers flush with the first chunk, settlement runs fire-and-forget inside the end wrapper, receipt header is structurally impossible ('headers already flushed; payment-response receipt not attached' - vendor's own stderr). Buyer receives the full value, pays in full, holds nothing naming the transaction; combined with P1 the primary agent endpoint shape cannot reconcile lost-response retries

scenarios.name: silent-v3-downgrade
scenarios.checks: tokenVersion:3 against a pre-v3 backend: the field is dropped without error (whitelist semantics), a reusable v2 token returns. detectAccessTokenVersion reports the true version (good contract, documented), but the downgrade path emits no warning and the default mint is v2 regardless - a buyer who wanted single-use semantics silently holds a reusable credential if they forget to branch

scenarios.name: controls
scenarios.checks: C1 clean buffered v3 purchase: 1 service, 1 settlement, verifiable receipt attached. C3 buyer disconnect before delivery: honestly not charged - the middleware probes actual socket delivery via a byte-delta baseline rather than trusting status codes (handler work wasted remains the seller's cost). C4 empty balance: rejected by verify pre-handler, no delivery, no burn

findings_summary.title: Lost-response retry double-charges on the default v2 token: no idempotency key, no settlement query, receipt attached only to the lost response

Single-use enforcement is per-process and reactive: concurrent race delivers a free service; the guard arms only after witnessing BCK.X402.0059; multi-replica sellers have no guard at all (disclosed in source comment, not in seller-facing docs)

Any settle failure except 0059 delivers the resource unpaid with a console-only record - including the documented 200 + success:false shape, which even receives a settlement receipt; x402 path lacks the onPaymentError notification the MPP path has
Verify does not reserve credits: depletion between verify and settle delivers the second service free (insufficient-credits is not special-cased)
Streamed responses carry no settlement receipt ever (headers flushed) and settle is fire-and-forget after close - reconciliation impossible on the dominant agent endpoint shape
Silent v3->v2 downgrade on mint: SDK detects and returns the true version but emits no warning; default mint is v2 anyway

records.notes: Scope: real-SUT battery against a published npm SDK with an offline adversarial-facilitator mock implementing ONLY vendor-documented semantics; no vendor-operated service touched. Verdict taxonomy: FAIL = economic-loss window reproduced at runtime (service delivery and credit settlement decouple without a reconciliation path); HOLD = guard held as designed; DX = developer-experience gap without direct economic loss in the tested path. Venue status: draft issue prepared (pack: issue-sbs20-settlement-reconciliation.md), NOT yet filed - this seal attests the battery results, not an upstream disposition. Registry extension S-BS-20 (34 -> 35) ships to docs/block-b/REGISTRY.md as a post-merge patch. Relatives: S-BS-19 (same battery class, other SUT), S-BS-14/15 (verify/settle race axis, x402#3920), S-BS-06 (overcharge, x402#3866).

scenarios.checks: 10/10 PASS on MemoryBackend, public API only, expectations pre-registered (probe headers + battery README) before the run. W0 baseline replay (1 charge, identical result); W1a F1 default — retry re-raises the post-commit throw, 2 charges (the documented at-least-once window); W1b F1 opt-in isRetryable:false — 1 charge + IdempotencyUncertainError, blocked until forget(); W2a live lease never taken (IdempotencyInFlightError, executor not started); W2b expired-lease conditional takeover exactly once, then replay; W2c opt-in onLeaseExpired:'uncertain' — blocked until reconcile; W3 cross-instance race — 1 charge, loser gets InFlight, its retry replays the winner's result; W4 same key / different payload — IdempotencyConflictError on replay and in-flight paths (canonical SHA-256 fingerprint, key-order-insensitive; verifyRequest:false restores 0.1.x behavior); W5 pre-effect failure — retry commits exactly once; W6 TTL boundary — replay inside TTL, re-execute past TTL. Before-state contrast: all four before-discriminators (lost response, dead-holder takeover, cross-instance race, request-meta) reproduce the old behavior at 4d665ae — 4/4 OBSERVED-BEFORE.

findings_summary.title: Lost response after commit: executor commits the effect at the provider, then throws — a retry re-fires the committed side effect and both calls see a clean error. Root cause @ 4d665ae: failures are not cached and the state machine has no committed/uncertain state ('throw => nothing happened'), store.ts:95-112. FIXED in v0.2.0: documented at-least-once default, isRetryable gives callers an explicit contract (W1a/W1b PASS). Verified-fixed.

Crash after commit: a dead holder's pending row is unconditionally reset by the next caller (memory.ts:60-71, postgres.ts:72-77 @ 4d665ae), re-executing a committed effect under the guise of 'crash recovery'. FIXED in v0.2.0: lease-based liveness — takeover requires lease expiry (W2a/W2b/W2c PASS). Verified-fixed.

Cross-instance race: two store instances on one shared backend (advertised multi-instance topology) — the claim loser resets the winner's LIVE pending row and re-runs; both execute the effect and both return success with different results. FIXED in v0.2.0: lease/ownership guards (W3 PASS). Before-state probe modeled the documented PostgresBackend contract; v0.2.0 Postgres SQL itself was not executed (maintainer-scope caveat).

Coordinated disclosure to maintainer Tripl3 before publication; credited in the project's SECURITY.md ('Igor (Argus agent test lab)'). External verification note published (gist 9ea3f09a18e50b2bb590123b1134902b) and to be linked from the project's release notes/SECURITY.md per maintainer agreement.

records.notes: Scope (kept explicit at the maintainer's request): (1) the ten-window battery ran on MemoryBackend — it verifies the store/runOnce logic, not the Postgres SQL (Postgres-specific coverage is planned by the maintainer); (2) F1 semantics — the default still allows the documented at-least-once window, isRetryable is what closes it; the battery verifies the classification and its documentation, not an unconditional exactly-once. The ten-window battery harness and its pre-registered expectations live in the lab's verification environment (scripts intentionally not vendored upstream; available on request — same promise as the original report); the before-state probe harness and both run records ARE pinned as evidence, and the suite cross-checks are reproducible from the public repo. Remaining documented edge: DB-clock lease expiry planned for 0.3.0 (backend-interface change); README documents the event-loop-blocking (>leaseMs lease loss) and clock-drift sizing traps (b1d96fd). This seal covers the T1 engagement end-to-end: before-state reproduction (2026-10-26), coordinated disclosure, v0.2.0 ten-window verification (2026-10-27), publication, and the pre-seal re-verification on the lab VM (2026-10-28).
